01 — The idea

Ideas are easy. Building and keeping them alive isn't.

Most people have ideas. Turning an idea into reality is one problem. Sustaining it once it exists is a different problem entirely. Zebraish is a two door company built to solve both. Studio is door one, it takes an idea and builds it into something real. The Board is door two, it helps that business actually understand and keep its customers. Fashion is a third door, its own creative world under the same company.

Studio and The Board together are the two doors, the part of Zebraish built for someone who already knows how to run a real business.

Studio
Build Engine
Sharpens an idea into a real, working app or website. Mostly for people building software startups.
● Real, today
See MoreSee Less ⌄
Who it's for

Studio takes a raw idea and sharpens it into something real, a working app or website, built properly. It's mostly built for people launching a software business, but it also works for anyone standing at the edge of an idea with no team yet, an early business still figuring itself out, a small business still running everything by hand, or an existing company that has outgrown its basic website. The common thread is simple, someone has something worth building and doesn't yet have the team to build it.

The process

Every engagement moves through the same ten stages, idea, discovery, strategy, design, build, launch, automate, market, measure, grow. Discovery is where Studio actually listens, what the idea is, who it's for, what already exists, what's missing. Strategy turns that into a real plan, what the first version needs to contain, what can wait, what technology actually makes sense. Design and build turn the plan into a working product, and launch is where it goes live. From there, automate and market build the machinery that keeps the business running without constant manual effort, and measure and grow close the loop, feeding straight into The Board, where the business gets discovered and starts actually learning from its customers.

None of this hands off between disconnected vendors. It's one team, holding the full context from the first conversation through to the business standing on its own.

What we build

Build covers the product itself, websites, apps, software, whatever the idea actually needs to exist. Intelligence means smart tools and data, but only where it actually solves a problem, never added just to sound impressive. Automate removes the repetitive manual work that quietly caps how far a business can grow before it even notices the ceiling. Brand gives the business an identity, the difference between "I have an idea" and "I have something that looks and feels like a real company." And Grow is the handoff, launch strategy and the direct connection into The Board, where the business starts learning from the people it's actually built for.

Why not a freelancer

A freelancer sells hours or a fixed package, delivers a site, and disappears, no connection to what happens after launch, and no path back in when something new is needed. Studio stays connected through the whole lifecycle. Launch flows straight into The Board, and if the business later needs a rebuild, a new automation or a new product, it comes straight back into Studio. Studio and The Board aren't two separate vendors, they're one loop, and that loop is the actual product.

The Board
Business Ecosystem
Helps businesses truly understand their customers, all in one place, plus real business analytics.
● Prototype
See MoreSee Less ⌄
What it is

The Board is the second door. After a business is built with Studio, The Board is where it learns how to actually understand its customers and manage what comes next, still under Zebraish. It's a global, all in one feedback platform. Customers drop honest reviews, hot takes and wishlists in one place, and companies can drop their own new plans and ideas to see, in real time, whether their customers actually want them. There's no single app that brings a business and its customers this close together.

Businesses should be able to go viral

Social media changed what it took for an unknown person to be seen — someone could make one good thing, post it, and go from nobody to somebody without needing money, connections or a media team behind them. The Board is built on the same idea, applied to businesses. A small company with something genuinely good shouldn't need a massive ad budget or celebrity backing just to be noticed — it should be able to get discovered because people are actually responding to what it's building.

The vocabulary

Users don't submit generic "feedback" — they hype what's good, cap what isn't, and drop receipts: structured bug reports, feature requests and complaints the community can vote on. A Hype is an upvote, a Cap is a downvote, a Receipt is structured feedback, a Drip is a free-form community post, and when a signal's hype is accelerating fast enough, it's Going Flame — impossible for the business to ignore.

For the business

Every complaint and request becomes ranked, structured data instead of noise, a Health Score for the business, a flame ranked wishlist of what people actually want built next, and a public status that moves from Open through Seen, Planned, Building and Built. Businesses also get access to real business analytics tools, so instead of guessing what to build next based on internal politics and whoever talks loudest in the room, they can see exactly what their customers want.

Status

The Board is designed and demonstrable, the architecture, data model and product flows are fully worked out, but it isn't live yet. It's a prototype, not a claim about customers or revenue that don't exist.

Fashion
Creative Universe
Creative luxury outfits, built with a friend in Barcelona.
● Prototype
See MoreSee Less ⌄
Not just zebra print

It would be easy to read Zebraish Fashion as a brand that puts zebra stripes on clothes — that's far too narrow a read. It's an animal-inspired fashion universe, where the animal world becomes a creative vocabulary: pattern, texture, skin, coat, fur, feather, color, silhouette and material, not just print. The zebra is the flagship because it's the animal the whole company's name and identity comes from, and it appears more prominently than any other animal in the system — but the brand isn't imprisoned by it. Zebra is the foundation; other animals expand the universe around it, which gives the brand room to grow creatively for years without repeating the same striped garment.

The look we're going for

Animal skin is the inspiration, not a print to copy. These are references for the direction, not the collection itself.

The animal family

Each animal contributes its own design vocabulary, not just its pattern. Zebra brings black and white, sharp contrast and bold, graphic rhythm. Giraffe brings irregular geometric markings in warm browns, tan and cream, with a more organic, elongated feel. Leopard brings spots and rosettes, high-contrast patterning and a sense of predatory luxury. Snake brings scales, glossy surfaces and a dark, fluid, sometimes metallic visual language. Birds bring feathers, plumage and flight — lightness, layering and unusual color combinations that go well beyond anything printed on fabric. The goal in every case is the same: make the garment feel like it belongs to the animal, not like the animal's pattern was pasted onto it.

The collaboration

This vertical is being built with a friend of mine, an influencer based in Barcelona, to produce lovely, creative luxury outfits. It's its own conversation, running in parallel to this one, and it's a real, active collaboration, not a placeholder.

Status

The creative universe and animal system are fully defined, but Fashion isn't live yet — it's a prototype, shown here so you see the complete picture of what Zebraish is building, not just the technology half.
